extracted.intended_audience: postdoctoral researchers applying for NIH K99/R00 (and reviewers/readers of K99/R00 proposals)
extracted.subtask_description: A postdoctoral K99/R00 career development and research proposal describing candidate training, independence plan, timelines, specific aims, preliminary data, and research strategy in cytoskeletal biology/aging. Intended to justify funding for transition to independent PI.

rubrics_metrics.name: Teaching proficiency and commitment
rubrics_metrics.description: Many high school, undergraduate, masters, and graduate students in and out of the lab, which I believe make me proficient in teaching. I am also highly invested in increasing the presence of under-represented minority in STEM, and have been involved directly in programs focused in this cause including the NIH Bridges to Baccalaureate (B2B) program and the CHORI Summer Research program.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Provide concrete mentoring/teaching experience across levels (high school through graduate), involvement in outreach/diversity programs (e.g., B2B, CHORI), and plans to evolve similar programs at the future institute. Anticipate and address criticism that teaching reduces research dedication by arguing teaching preserves and expands research excellence.

rubrics_metrics.name: Independence from mentor
rubrics_metrics.description: Dr. Dillin ... maintains open communications, open availability of strains and resources, and complete transparency to avoid scientific overlap. My work on cytoskeletal biology is unique in the Dillin lab, ... Dr. Dillin has also assured me that I am free to take any reagents and strains I need to establish my own lab, and that the scientific discoveries I make during the K99 phase will intellectually belong to me.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Demonstrate clear plan and assurances for intellectual independence: minimal scientific overlap with mentor, access to reagents/resources for startup, written/verbal mentor commitments to avoid overlap and allow trainees to take materials and intellectual ownership.

rubrics_metrics.name: Plan for Career Development / Training Activities
rubrics_metrics.description: Throughout the award period, I will direct a majority of my time to the proposed research. My previous scientific training has been focused on understanding cell biology and genetics. This additional training will expand my experimental skillsets to data science, including understanding large transcriptome, ChIP-seq, ATAC-seq, and proteome datasets.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Lay out explicit training goals and how they will be achieved (e.g., hands-on work with labs/mentors, coursework), with focus areas (mass spectrometry, bioinformatics, large-data methods). Allocate majority effort to research while documenting training activities that expand technical and analytic skills.

rubrics_metrics.name: Mass spectrometry training
rubrics_metrics.description: Learn more about mass spectrometry: my training in biochemistry is limited, and I plan to address this issue during the K99 award period by working closely with the Ting lab to develop an assay for proximity labeling of molecular interactors of actin. I will educate myself by reading instructional text, such as Mass Spectrometry for Biotechnology by Gary Suizdak, and I will also take instructional lessons at the Proteomic core at UC Davis.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: State concrete training steps (reading texts, hands-on core lessons, mentorship with an expert lab) to gain competency in a new technical area required for the proposed research.

rubrics_metrics.name: Bioinformatics training
rubrics_metrics.description: As a cell biologist and geneticist, my skillsets in bioinformatics are basic. Thus, I will spend a large amount of time with a post-doc in the lab, Dr. Raz Bar-Ziv, who is an expert in bioinformatics techniques using Galaxy and Matlab. I have already begun training with him in understanding how to analyze transcriptome datasets, and will continue to expand my knowledge by training with him and members of the Eisen lab to learn how to apply these techniques to other large datasets, including ChIP-seq and ATAC-seq. I also plan to take Databases and tools of Bioinformatics offered by the UC Berkeley learning center.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Document planned mentorship-based training, named collaborators/mentors, software/tools to learn (Galaxy, Matlab), and formal coursework to substantiate acquisition of bioinformatics skills.

rubrics_metrics.name: Collaborations and advisory panel
rubrics_metrics.description: I have designed a scientific advisory panel including experts in diverse fields within the San Francisco Bay Area. I will work directly with the members of these labs, and have committee meetings every 6-9 months during the K99 phase. We will work on my scientific progress, career development, and future publication and grant applications.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Include an advisory committee with named experts, schedule regular meetings (e.g., every 6–9 months), and describe roles: review progress, advise on career development, assist with publications and grant planning.

rubrics_metrics.name: Teaching and mentoring experience as career training
rubrics_metrics.description: Within the Dillin lab, I will continue to mentor students on several levels: I currently have two graduate students, two undergraduate students, and one full-time technician that work in my team. ... I will continue to train these and any additional students that I acquire. I will also take the time to continue working with Dr. Dillin in his molecular genetics lab in designing and carrying out a laboratory course.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use existing trainee supervision plus opportunities to design/run courses as evidence of training toward PI teaching responsibilities; document numbers/levels of trainees and specific teaching roles (TA, adjunct, course design).

rubrics_metrics.name: Increasing diversity in STEM (career training and service)
rubrics_metrics.description: A large goal of mine is to increase the diversity – both of underrepresented minorities and underrepresented socioeconomic groups – in STEM. Currently, I am part of the B2B program at UC Berkeley ... I am also part of the CHORI/CIRM summer research program ... I will work with the heads of these programs to increase my involvement, but also to learn how to incorporate these types of programs into my future institute.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Describe active involvement in recruitment/mentoring programs for underrepresented groups, roles on selection committees, and plans to scale or implement such programs at the candidate's future institution.

rubrics_metrics.name: Lab management skills
rubrics_metrics.description: I have a large amount of management experience both in restaurants and in retail. ... I was serving as a secondary laboratory manager. Currently in the Dillin lab, I am expanding my expertise in lab management by working with our exceptional lab manager ... as he teaches me how to manage finances, personnel, and inventory of a lab. Moreover, he allows me to engage in direct negotiations with vendors.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Show concrete experience and mentorship in lab administrative tasks: budgeting, personnel management, inventory, vendor negotiations; describe how these experiences prepare candidate to run an independent lab.

rubrics_metrics.name: Writing and grant-writing experience
rubrics_metrics.description: I have had the fortune of being given the freedom to write my manuscripts independently ... I have also written multiple grants both for myself, my students, and with Dr. Dillin, and write all progress reports for several grants, including my independent F32 and an R01 that I co-authored with Dr. Dillin. I will continue to expand my writing skills by co-authoring future R01 and R21-level grants.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: List prior independent writing (manuscripts, grants, progress reports) and concrete plans to continue co-authoring larger grants as evidence of preparedness for independent funding.

rubrics_metrics.name: Timelines for career benchmarks
rubrics_metrics.description: Timelines for Career Benchmarks: detailed timeline spanning pre-award, K99 years, and R00 years with milestone goals such as completing postdoc projects, submitting and revising manuscripts, beginning proximity labeling, acquiring faculty position offer, lab set up and hiring, teaching responsibilities, submitting R01/R21, and securing R01.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Provide a detailed, dated timeline with concrete milestone goals (papers, project completions, faculty job search, lab setup, grant submissions) showing realistic pacing for transition to independence.

rubrics_metrics.name: Specific Aims clarity and hypotheses
rubrics_metrics.description: Aim 1: How does chromatin remodeling and lipid homeostasis regulate actin organization and function? Aim 2: What is the nature of the neuronal communication to preserve the cytoskeleton in distal tissues via non-autonomous HSF-1? Aim 3: What is the molecular nature of the cytoskeleton resulting in major tissue-specific differences in cytoskeletal form and function?
rubrics_metrics.guidance: State a small number (typically 2–3) of focused, testable Specific Aims with clear hypotheses, rationale, and how results will address gaps in knowledge.

rubrics_metrics.name: Significance
rubrics_metrics.description: The actin cytoskeleton ... is required for a diverse array of cellular pathways ... The mechanisms involved in preservation of cytoskeletal form and function are not well understood. ... This work will not only increase the understanding of genes and proteins required for cytoskeletal preservation, but will increase the understanding of the requirement of actin filament structure and function in the collapse of homeostasis and health during organismal aging.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Explain the importance of the problem, gaps in current knowledge, and how the proposed work will advance the field (biological and/or clinical impact).

rubrics_metrics.name: Innovation
rubrics_metrics.description: My currently proposed studies are unique in that I use these novel tools to directly identify genes essential for cytoskeletal regulation. Moreover, I propose to adapt these tools even further for utility in biochemical assays ... I have the platforms for direct interrogation of the requirement of identified hits in regulation of actin under normal and aging physiologies.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Highlight novel tools, methods, or conceptual advances (e.g., LifeAct in C. elegans, adaptation to biochemical assays) and explain why approaches offer significant advantages over prior work.

rubrics_metrics.name: Preliminary data and feasibility
rubrics_metrics.description: I have created a system to interrogate cytoskeletal quality in vivo in C. elegans ... I performed the first comprehensive analysis of changes to actin filaments during aging in C. elegans. ... I have shown direct evidence for cytoskeletal maintenance and that hsf-1 is required for maintenance of the actin cytoskeleton during aging.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Provide preliminary results demonstrating feasibility of key methods and initial findings that justify the proposed studies (e.g., transgenics, imaging, genetic perturbations).

rubrics_metrics.name: Research Plan: multi-pronged genetic screening approach
rubrics_metrics.description: I employed multi-pronged genetic screening: (1) in vivo live-cell imaging of actin filaments to identify transcription factors, (2) whole genome synthetic lethality screening with hsf-1 mutants in C. elegans, (3) transcriptome analysis after sub-lethal actin knockdown, and (4) whole genome CRISPR-Cas9 screening in human BJ fibroblasts under cytochalasin D.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use complementary screening approaches across models and assay types to identify candidate regulators; clearly describe each method and how results will be integrated.

rubrics_metrics.name: Screen cross-referencing and validation
rubrics_metrics.description: Cross-referencing these rich datasets has revealed two critical nodes of genes: 1) modifiers of chromatin state ... and 2) genes involved in lipid storage and lipid homeostasis. The identification of various genes with overlapping functions across the screens provides a high level of confidence in these datasets.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Demonstrate overlap across independent screens to increase confidence in hits; perform secondary and tertiary validation assays for candidates identified in primary screens.

rubrics_metrics.name: Proximity labeling biochemical interrogation of actin interactome
rubrics_metrics.description: We propose to employ biochemical interrogation of cytoskeletal interactors by utilizing proximity labeling methods combined with LifeAct and miniTurbo technology. Goals: (1) identification of novel molecular interactors of actin required for cytoskeletal maintenance, (2) characterization of differences in cytoskeletal regulators across tissues, and (3) characterization of the loss of cytoskeletal interactors that result in breakdown during aging.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Describe specific biochemical approaches (e.g., proximity labeling with miniTurbo), intended analyses (identification and tissue-specific comparison of interactors), and how these assays connect to in vivo phenotypes and aging.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use of appropriate models and perturbations
rubrics_metrics.description: In vivo LifeAct imaging in C. elegans muscle, intestine, hypodermis; synthetic lethality RNAi in hsf-1 mutants; transcriptome RNAseq after 10% act-1 RNAi; CRISPR-Cas9 screening in BJ fibroblasts with 0.25 µM cytochalasin D.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Select model organisms/cell lines and perturbations that are appropriate to the question; document dosages/conditions and rationalize cross-species approaches for conserved mechanisms.

rubrics_metrics.name: Sequencing and sgRNA distribution analysis for screen readouts
rubrics_metrics.description: CRISPR-Cas9 screening: sequencing and sgRNA distribution analysis to identify enriched and depleted genes (e.g., 363 genes enriched, 198 genes depleted). RNAseq: tRNA collection, 450 genes upregulated and 192 genes downregulated.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use appropriate high-throughput sequencing analyses and distribution/scoring metrics to call hits from pooled screens and transcriptome studies; report sensitivity thresholds and result counts as evidence of screen performance.
